items.text: From this update onward, update information for all platforms will be consolidated into a single set of notes.
Items marked [All Platforms] apply to every platform.
Please note that the Nintendo Switch 2 version is currently under review, and as such, its update is expected to be released later than on other platforms.
Story
An issue in Episode 2 wherein lamps corresponding to unobtained Melodies would light up on the Bonboya Gate has been addressed.
The progression requirements from Episode 2 to Episode 3 have been changed.
Encounter events with certain enemies have been removed from the progression conditions.
1.1.14 Hotfix Onward Episode 3 Progression Requirements [Gameplay Info / Spoilers]
The following section includes specific character names and detailed steps. Please skip this section if you wish to avoid gameplay spoilers.

notes.title: In Episode 2, the following two conditions must be met

items.text: ① For each of the following four Dark Ratatan, trigger their fifth encounter event, win that World’s boss battle, and obtain a Melody:
・Reek N. Roll
・Bork the Biter
・Funky Fang
・Midnight Knight
One Melody will be obtained from each of them in the event after winning the battle.
If defeated, that Dark Ratatan will reappear in World 1 on subsequent adventures until defeated.
② Trigger Tangletung’s fifth encounter event and obtain one Melody.
Once these conditions are met, five Melody lamps will light up on the Bonboya Gate.
Clear World 5 of Episode 2 in that state.
After the event, return to Rataport to unlock the option to select Episode 3.
An issue wherein purchased DLC was not being applied correctly in-game has been addressed.
Even if the DLC has already been purchased, the corresponding items and content will be granted correctly after updating.
We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused.
Resolved Issues
DLC
Fixed an issue where purchased and activated DLC was not being applied correctly in-game.
Players who have already purchased the DLC will receive the corresponding items and content after updating.
We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused.
Added voice and sound effects to Dark Ratatan battles.
Updated the credits (thank you for everyone’s patience!).
If you couldn’t find your name, please send us an email at support@ratata-arts.com
Fixed an issue where Cobun would stop moving and halt progress under specific conditions, such as during the Target Timer.
Fixed an issue in the Altar Hall where the Healing Fountain would overlap with the Altar.
Note: The Healing Fountain will no longer appear in the Altar Hall.
Fixed an issue where visual effects were not displaying correctly for certain attacks.
Fixed an issue where the normal attack damage multiplier from Nyandola's Super Fever Tech "Mew Mew Mania" was not applied to 'Good' judgments in Rhythm Commands.
Fixed an issue in World 1 where Squidly Pete's pull attack would trigger even when frozen.
Fixed an issue where the settings for Decorune attached to accessories dropped by Dark Ratatan in Episode 2 did not function correctly.
Fixed an issue where the game crashed upon launch on Steam Deck.
Please note that as Steam Deck and Linux are not currently officially supported, this is a provisional fix.

We have received feedback that players are unable to proceed to Episode 2 or that the unlock conditions are unclear. We apologize for the inconvenience. To unlock Episode 2, the following two conditions must be met:
Clear Episode 1 (Complete up to World 5 for the first time)
Raise the "Goddess’ Game" Oath Level to 1 or higher
After applying this update, you will be able to proceed by starting the game with the above conditions met.
Scenario
Fixed an issue where Episode 2 would sometimes not appear even if the conditions were met.
Fixed an issue in the Episode 2 tutorial where the text condition "Raise Covenant Level to 1 or higher" was not displayed in some languages.
Stage Gimmicks / Demos
Fixed an issue in Episode 2 where the animation for "Dark Ratatan" appearing was not displayed correctly.
Fixed an issue in Episode 2 where BGM would overlap if the "Dark Ratatan" demo occurred during an interval.
As a temporary measure, only the original interval BGM will play.
We plan to implement a dedicated BGM for this in a future update.
Fixed an issue where Ratatan was able to move at the start of the ending.
Fixed an issue where the playback conditions for some Tangletung demos were unintended.
Ratakaruta
Ratakaruta Duo "Ice Blight"
Fixed an issue where some enemies' HP would recover when unfreezing.
As a temporary measure for this fix, the following specification change has been made:
Change: HP reduction caused by this effect is no longer treated as "damage" by the system.
Impact: Effects such as those that "activate upon taking damage" will not apply.
We plan to revert this in a future update so that it is treated as normal "damage" again.
Network / Multiplayer
Shortened the phase transition time (the time from when the gate opens until movement begins).
Mitigated an issue where frequent disconnections from the session occurred in multiplayer games involving players in specific network environments.
We are currently investigating an issue where the game fails to launch on Steam Deck.
We plan to address this in a future update. We apologize for the inconvenience and appreciate your patience.

releases.displayName: Ratatan’s December Update: Descent of the Dark Ratatan

items.text: Hello, everyone!
We’d like to share the current progress on the next major update planned for December.
This update has been particularly challenging to develop, and we are currently aiming to release it around the end of December.
Once adjustments are finalized, we’ll publish detailed patch notes—so please look forward to them.
Additionally, this update connects directly to “To the Everafter”, planned for next spring.
From here, the story and challenges that lead toward all the Dark Ratatans—and ultimately the mysterious “??? Battles”—will finally begin to unfold.
We hope you’re excited for what’s coming!
In this update, we’ll be introducing new events and new battles related to the Dark Ratatan.

As mentioned previously, one of the major issues with the roguelite structure has been its over-reliance on battles, so we’re refining the experience to better balance battles and event-driven progression.
After clearing World 5, new story content will unfold as Episode 2.
The events are designed so players can gradually experience the lead-up to challenges such as Goddess Games and Formidable Foes.
Furthermore, the Dark Ratatan events are not just additional boss encounters—they play a central role in storytelling and touch on the core of Ratatan’s narrative.
They also function as roguelite events, evolving the structure so that story and gameplay become more closely integrated.
Regarding the new stage tricks and gimmicks shown previously on the roadmap:
For the December update, we decided to integrate these elements into the Dark Ratatan event side, in order to focus the design and development resources on delivering a cohesive experience.
The Dark Ratatan battles follow a structure unlike any previous boss fights in the game.
In addition to their own attacks, they command Dark Cobun through musical cues, mirroring Ratatan’s own command style.
The difficulty ranks among the highest in the entire game, and defeating them will reward players with powerful Mythic-tier gear.
Not all Dark Ratatans will appear in this update; they will be added gradually in future patches.
A major highlight of these battles is the new original track composed specifically for the Dark Ratatan, forming the core of the battle presentation.
We hope you enjoy this fresh musical experience.
A new system, Duo, is coming to Ratakaruta.
By raising the elemental forces of two or more attributes beyond a certain threshold, you’ll gain access to powerful Duo Ratakaruta.

notes.title: This expands deck-building possibilities in two directions

items.text: • Continued support for single-element builds
• New incentives for multi-element, hybrid builds
Because Duo cards are extremely powerful, the December update will limit acquisition to one per run.
We will continue monitoring balance and may adjust this limit in the future.
The Goddess Gacha allows players to convert unwanted equipment, accessories, and materials into points, which can then be used for gacha pulls.
Some exclusive items will appear only here, but the feature is intended as a light-hearted way to recycle surplus items.
We’re updating the online random match lobby to improve usability.
• Ability to enter any available room
• A refresh button for lobby listings
We are adding a new accessory rarity: Legendary.
These accessories include random Decorune effects, further enhancing strategic depth in build crafting.

items.text: Super Fever Skills now grant Super Armor.
Super Fever Skills will no longer be canceled by knockback or status effects caused by enemy attacks.
Improved gameplay experience by preventing the sudden drop in BGM intensity from reducing player enjoyment.

BGM now transitions smoothly with a fade after using a Super Fever Skill.
Extended the display time of item rewards after opening a treasure chest during 'Treasure Chance'.
In Random Match lobbies, players who remain inactive for 4 minutes will now automatically leave the lobby.
This prevents multiplayer sessions from starting due to idle players.
Added a message that appears when attempting to join a Random Match and no available rooms are found.
In multiplayer lobbies, the player who becomes the room owner will now have an owner icon displayed next to their status.
Fixed an issue where save data could be lost if it failed to load properly at startup.
Fixed a crash that could occur when freeze and burn effects were applied simultaneously.
Fixed an issue where certain visual effects did not display as intended.
Fixed a bug where obtaining Ratakaruta under specific conditions in multiplayer could cause an error.
Fixed an issue where Raindrop Hop would hit enemies and fail to explode upon ground impact.
Fixed COMtan’s movement speed when passing through the Goodie Gates in multiplayer.
Fixed an issue where interacting with a Treasure Chance chest after clearing a wave could become impossible until the player moved away from it once.
Fixed an issue where character voices sometimes failed to play correctly on the Ratatan selection screen when starting a new game.
Fixed an issue where the mouse wheel scroll amount was reduced.
Fixed an error that could occur when resuming from a suspend save while Fire Elemental Force was ready to activate.
Fixed an issue in Advanced (4beat) Input Mode where the Super Fever Skill command was not assigned and could not be used.
Fixed an issue in Advanced (4beat) Input Mode where the Super Fever Skill command guide did not display correctly.
Fixed an issue where changes to confirm button assignments in the Options menu were not properly reflected.
Fixed an issue where accessory names and other text were not displaying correctly.
Fixed an issue where save data could become corrupted and fail to load properly.
This occurred when the amount of data being saved grew too large after extended gameplay sessions, so we have increased the upper limit for the amount of data that can be saved.
We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience caused to all players.
We are also continuing to investigate an issue where save data deemed corrupted could be automatically deleted upon exiting the application. A fix for this issue is planned soon.
If your save data has already been lost, please follow the steps below to attempt recovery from Steam Cloud.

notes.title: Restoring Save Data from Steam Cloud

items.text: Close the game.
Log into Steam and access “store.steampowered.com/account/remotestorage”.
From the list, select “View Files” for Ratatan and download the following files:
RatataArts/Ratatan/xxxx/Ratatan1.rttn (if saved in slot 1)
RatataArts/Ratatan/xxxx/Ratatan2.rttn (if saved in slot 2)
RatataArts/Ratatan/xxxx/Ratatan3.rttn (if saved in slot 3)
RatataArts/Ratatan/xxxx/RatatanSys.rttn
If the downloaded files contain extra characters in their names, rename them as follows:
Ratatan1.rttn
Ratatan2.rttn
Ratatan3.rttn
RatatanSys.rttn

notes.title: Open Ratatan’s save data folder. It is usually located at

items.text: “C:\\Users\\(username)\\AppData\\LocalLow\\RatataArts\\Ratatan”.
Inside the folder, open the subfolder with the most recent modification date and a numeric name.
Move all downloaded save files into that folder.
If data already exists, overwrite it.
Launch the game and check if your save data has been restored.
If it has not been restored, try the steps again from the beginning or attempt using a different folder.
We have corrected the supported language display on the Steam store page from “Spanish – Spain” to “Spanish – Latin America.”
This change was made to resolve a discrepancy between the language shown on the store page and the actual language displayed in the game.
We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience caused by this labeling error.

This update addresses the CVE-2025-59489 vulnerability.

Added Frame Rate Cap
When vertical sync was turned off, the frame rate would increase excessively, causing high CPU usage. To address this, a frame rate cap has been implemented.
When vertical sync is off, the frame rate will now be capped at 240 FPS.
Rhythm Action Judgment Logic
We’ve adjusted the judgment logic for rhythm actions to reduce discrepancies between music and notes caused by system performance or load.
However, we must honestly inform you that this fix introduced a new issue where the de-sync can reoccur if the game is paused at certain timings.
While it’s not a perfect update, we chose to release it now to improve what we believe was the most frustrating issue for players.
We remain fully committed to resolving the remaining issues and welcome your continued feedback.

Hello RataTEAM!

First off thanks for the great feedback on the backer Beta. It's been invaluable for providing insight in areas we can focus on for improvement. Also, for those of you who didn't get a chance to play the Beta, we are cooking something up to allow more people the chance to play in the near future now that we have given precedence to our backers.

It's been over a year and a half since we launched our Ratatan Kickstarter campaign so we are going to slow down the frequency of updates. We have completed the closed Beta and are getting closer and closer to a release so we want to keep a few surprises up our sleeves.

notes.title: Scheduled Dates Listed in the Kickstarter Campaign

items.text: To everyone who has supported Ratatan, we can't thank you enough for your warm and continued support.

We apologize for the lack of explanation on our part regarding the Kickstarter delivery date being listed as April 2025. This led to a situation where that date was mistaken for a final release date. This date ws an estimate of when we expected to deliver rewards to our backers, but is not the official release date.
We are working diligently to prepare an official launch date for Ratatan and will make a clear announcement once a decision has been made.
We apologize for any inconvenience this has caused and will continue to make every effort to meet your expectations. Thank you for your continued support!

Now that the Closed Beta Test is over, the next step is to prepare for the open beta and early access. At this point, many issues still remain. Many have enjoyed the game, but there have also been some concerns and anxieties.

The development team will continue to address these issues and expand upon the game's content in preparation for the next milestone. We will also continue to add polish and new content even after early access. I'll explain our roadmap when the time comes.
Please know, we will continue to develop the game with the aim of making it a GOTY award-winning title.
Producer Kazuto Sakajiri
Introduction
This test was based on feedback we’d received and tested two major updates to improve quality.
Questionnaire Results
660/775（85.2%）Extremely Positive
The survey was collected in the same format as the Steam store. We had 7,361 activated keys, which means a response rate of approximately 10%. We were able to reach our testing goal of 85%.
Changes Per Update

The first release was unstable and lost much of its evaluation, and it took two updates and a lot of work to win it back. In order to achieve the overwhelmingly positive reception we ultimately hoped for, we had to further improve on quality and raise the level of that evaluation.

At the time of posting, we have Nyandola in first place, with Pyokorappa in second place, and Harigittan in third place.
It's still difficult to completely average out the popularity of every character, so we will do our best to shine a spotlight on the unpopular characters as well.
Hello RataTEAM!
It's update time and of course we have more information about the ongoing backer beta. It's a big update so grab a seat and have a read!

Ratatan will be taking part in The MIX Spring Showcase on March 17th during GDC week. The showcase is a digital event featuring news, reveals, announcements and more. The show kicks off at 9:00AM Pacific Time and can be viewed on the following channels:
YouTube / Twitch / Homepage
In this update, we're going to go over the Closed Beta Test that is currently underway and how it is progressing.
The main features of this supersized update will be the addition of World 2's Yeehawler Mountain and its boss the Wagoon, as well as the next Ratatan, Kamonelo and the new Wand wielding cobun.

Deep in the dry, windswept wilderness, a rail car once carried gilded treasures through the canyon. But now it's up to you to infiltrate Yeehawler Ranch, home of the roaming Wagoon, and seize its owner, Saguaro Slim!
This area's boss, Wagoon, will call out to the female Bessoons to help him when he's under attack, and has a habit of diving into the sand to attack you from below!
Character Introduction
Kamonelo (VA: Nonoka Obuchi)
Behind Kamonelo's blank expression, is a mind operating at speeds we can only imagine, pondering the world's complexities.
They’ll sometimes overthink and act in ways that are incomprehensible.
They enjoy looking at the sky.
"To fly or not to fly, that is likely the question."
"Oh, to be nice and empty, like the sky..."
Kamonelo’s cobun.
Proficient with a wand.

We have already received a lot of feedback from the Closed Beta test identifying many glitches and parts of the game with low useability. It's difficult to respond to all of these issues right away, so we're examining them one by one and will update the game to make it even better.
Please refer to the patch notes below for more details on this update.

World 2: Bad Day on Yeehawler Mountain is now available.: The boss, Wagoon, has a distinctive attack, such as summoning Bessoons to increase its attack capacity or diving into the sand to attack from below.: Once the Wagoon is defeated, the game can then be played in a circular fashion.

Added Kamonelo functionality to Ratatan: This Ratatan initially enters fights with Assault Cobun and Magical Cobun. The cobun's HP is restored slightly when the rhythm command gathers everyone together, so the troops can last longer if this cobun is utilized effectively.

Added the wand cobun class.: A long-range weapon, the wand's means of attack changes depending on the attributes of any implemented Ratakaruta.: The unit skill allows them to target enemies and gather in one place, or target an ally to boost their attack power.

It is now possible to input a rhythm command and move the Ratatan except while taking a performance motion.: An occurrence where the Ratatan was unable to act more than expected when failing a rhythm command input, etc., has been resolved.

The maximum number of cobun that can join an adventure has been changed from 6 to 9.: The maximum number of cobun will be expandable at the support desk in the future.: The number of cobun that can be taken by default is currently set in the player enhancement menu, but will be further expanded in the future.
When a cobun is caught by a monster or some other obstacle during the “Align” rhythm command, it will now slip through and return to the vicinity of the Ratatan.
The following enemy long-range attacks now display a marker on the target of the attack: Pointy Chief / Pinchy
Adjusted the HP, attack power, and action interval of Teshita or other enemies.
The arrows fired by Teshita's bow attacks have been made more visible.
The damage of the Jolly Hermit's great move Frenzied Fish Cannon has been adjusted.

The damage reduction percentage during the effects of the rhythm command "Guard" has been increased. Also, while under the effect of Guard, the player will no longer be knocked back even if hit by an attack that would typically do so.

We have adjusted the amount of experience gained per material when leveling up weapons through crafting.: The amount of experience gained at level 1 has been adjusted, making it easier to level up overall.
We've removed boss materials from the Exchanger that were registered as items that could be exchanged for general-purpose material and other items.

Boss materials are dropped when a boss is defeated (there are multiple drops, one of which is dropped at random), and weapons that can be crafted using those materials also have a low probability of dropping when that same boss is defeated.
What will happen when using the "Skill 1" and "Skill 2" rhythm commands can now be confirmed on the composition screen.
The functions and how they are represented in the Craft Menu, Inventory, and Organization screens have been unified, such as those for equipped and the item lock function.
Added text to the call icons on the inventory, organization screen, and pause menu to indicate which menus can be called.
After the appearance of NPCs at the Support Desk, My Room, Exchanger, and Crafting, will now only describe their facilities the first time you interact with them.
The fourth beat in the line indicating beats in the rhythm gauge has been removed.
The Rhythm Command Guide is now displayed when adventuring.: The display can be turned on or off in the options.
Added explanation text for items and choruses that can be acquired during an adventure.
Changed the cobun response voice when failing a rhythm command.
Fixed a bug where Hermit's great move Frenzied Fish Cannon was sometimes triggered at a time where it could not be dodged by the rhythm command.
Fixed a bug in which some tutorials would not play when starting the game again after being interrupted.

Hello! Producer Sakajiri, here.
This month we'd like to share some details about the long-awaited closed beta test.
Wishlists Now Exceed 100,000!
Thanks to your tremendous support, the number of wishlists on our Steam page is now more than 100,000! Thank you so much.

We've also received over 100 ratings for the Ratatan Original Soundtrack Demo, all of which have been positive. This is super encouraging for everyone on the department team, and we are working hard every day to create something that meets and hopefully exceeds your expectations.

About the Date for Closed Beta Test: Provided we don't hit any major obstacles, the Beta is scheduled to start on February 27, 2025. The distribution of codes, start date, and time will be announced via Discord and X as soon as they are confirmed.: However, we have sadly decided to forego the upcoming Steam Next Fest. Instead, we have made the decision to prioritize the closed beta test, and plan to better prepare a demo that will be available to the general public at the next Steam Next festival in June.: We look forward to your continued support and encouragement as we continue to develop this project ahead of a major rollout that will come in the summer.

Beta Test Overview: When the closed beta test is released, up to the end of Stage 1 is planned to be playable in the initial build. The test period is expected to last roughly one month with multiple updates throughout, including the addition of Stages 2 and 3 and more Ratatan, as well as extra features.: We will also provide a survey form during the test, so please feel free to give us your honest opinions and suggestions so that we can improve the quality of the game. We have reviewed all the feedback we have received so far and incorporated it into our plans, but it can take a long time before that feedback is reflected. We appreciate your understanding.

Items for Consideration: We have received many opinions and suggestions regarding command inputs. Rest assured, the team is aware of these and is considering them.: In addition to these, we'd like for players to do things like switch button combinations and show/hide guides in the options menu. We are preparing to test this as much as possible during the closed beta.
Test Precautions
We ask that you please participate in the beta with courtesy and within our guidelines.
Many glitches will be present due to the nature of the beta build. Please be aware that these may impede your ability to play the game.
There is still a possibility of mis-synchronization and connection problems when it comes to multiplayer.
Communication data from this test will be collected to improve the multiplayer experience.

Requests: Due to the postponement of participation in the Steam Next Fest, we ask that participants please refrain from taking screenshots and videos of the game, and distributing them or posting them on social media. However, you may share the information in the official Ratatan Discord. If you are a member of the media or a distributor, then please contact our management.

Introduction
This is a report on the alpha test we conducted in November.
This test was limited to a maximum of 500 people.

The alpha ROM was tested with many glitches in multiplayer and other areas, and we believe that there were many areas where players could not enjoy the game properly. However, we were able to get a lot of responses through our survey. Thank you all very much for your help!
Survey Results
The survey was obtained in the same format as the Steam store.
122/127 (96% favorable)

Since the test participants consisted only of backers, we fully understand that favorable result might be a little biased, but we feel very encouraged that so many of you were able to recognize our hard work. As mentioned earlier, there are still a number of glitches and areas that have not been adjusted properly, which has shown us again that we must tighten our focus in our development efforts.
Feedback from Test Participants and Response Guidelines

We have identified several issues by analyzing the many comments we received. We have determined that not all of them require major adjustments, but simply a bit of polish. The following three major guidelines are used to guide our response to these issues:
Remove inconveniences and absurdities
Remove incomprehensibility
Improve the rhythm command experience
Remove Inconveniences and Absurdities
The game was lacking in areas that were mainly caused by development reasons, and we're considering adjusting the following issues:
Hermit's beam attack and other big moves have been adjusted so that they are made in time with the rhythm.
Relax the rigidity of the rhythm command inputs.
When a rhythm command fails, make it possible to input the rhythm command from the next musical bar.
In the craft menu, implement a function to disassemble weapons and convert them into material items that can be used for crafting.
Remove Incomprehensibility
While we believe that a small tutorial is necessary, we intend to design the game so it can be played without a tutorial or explanation.
Reorganize the in-game UI to show if troop skills can be used in relation to the amount of MP remaining.
Adjust the in-game store so that an item's effect can be checked when hovering over it.
Review the response when a Ratatan is attacked.
Add wording to the description of material items in the inventory to indicate what they are used for.
Display the type and quantity of material items required for each item in the player enhancement menu, support desk menu, and crafting menu.
Add a guide highlighting interactable objects, items, and NPCs when approaching them at certain distances, etc.
Improve the Rhythm Command Experience
As a guideline for play after the beta, we would like to make it possible to realize various play styles by combining Ratatan x Cobun (weapon type) x Rhythm Command.
First of all, we are planning to give unique abilities (i.e. Ratatan abilities) for each Ratatan.
Abilities that enhance the effect of specific rhythm commands.
Abilities that provide a bonus for successful rhythm input, such as just-in-time inputs.
Those that give permanent abilities, etc..
In this way, the abilities will vary from Ratatan to Ratatan. This is how we intend to individualize the play style of each Ratatan in the game.

Next, for Cobun, we will add specific effects to troop skills, such as making it easier to destroy forts and such, or to blow up enemies and cancel their actions, as a means of differentiating between vanguard, mid-guard, and rear-guard troop types. We would like to make changing troop types and skills more meaningful in terms of gameplay than we have before.
Finally, for the rhythm commands, organizing what each command does and clarifying its role will make the effect of including the appropriate rhythm command in each situation more precise.

Taken together, these measures will help to realize the combination of Ratatan and Cobun by correctly judging their play style and inputting rhythm commands. We are planning to implement each of these measures for the beta, and we hope that you will join the rhythm action in the beta version once again.
Now, this is not to say that all of the above will be addressed as described above. We will also be adding content, fixing bugs, and adjusting the matching system in preparation for the beta test.
Although there are only a few days left until the beta test is upon us, the team will do its utmost to deliver an even better experience.

[DIRECTOR'S NOTE]
Something that likely caught your medama in this update is the implementation of the long awaited Ratatan, Pyokorappa, and the Assault Cobun.

The Assault Cobun is a lance user and the second in the vanguard class, but while it attacks aggressively with its lance from a certain distance, it does not have as high HP as the Soldier Cobun and is vulnerable to being shot.
It's an aggressive class that can keep attacking without taking damage by utilizing the formation command and pulling them back near your Ratatan as needed, so please give it a try.
We are also working on fixing bugs as needed based on the reports we receive. The fixes are being made in order of severity, starting with crashes, freezes, and anything blocking player progress.

Alongside this, we are also working on improving the synchronization of Ratatan's online multiplayer, but this is still in progress. We have confirmed that some problems may occur as a result of a combination of multiple factors, and will likely require a little more time.
